exercises.objective: Apply universal instantiation to a quantified sentence with given constants.
exercises.prompt: Given $\forall x:\text{Student}(x)\Rightarrow\text{MustAttend}(x)$ and the constant $\text{Priya}$, write the universally-instantiated ground sentence.
hints: Universal instantiation replaces the quantified variable $v$ with a concrete ground term $g$, via $\text{Subst}(\{v/g\},\alpha)$.
$\text{Student}(\text{Priya})\Rightarrow\text{MustAttend}(\text{Priya})$: the same sentence with every occurrence of $x$ replaced by $\text{Priya}$.

exercises.objective: Compute the unifying substitution for two atomic sentences.
hints: Match the sentences argument by argument: the first arguments are $\text{Prof}$ and $y$; the second arguments are $x$ and $\text{Robotics}$.
For the first arguments to become identical, $y$ must be substituted with $\text{Prof}$. For the second arguments, $x$ must be substituted with $\text{Robotics}$.

$\theta=\{x/\text{Robotics},\ y/\text{Prof}\}$. Check: $\text{Teaches}(\text{Prof},\text{Robotics})=\text{Teaches}(\text{Prof},\text{Robotics})$, identical, confirming $\theta$ unifies the two sentences.

exercises.objective: Apply Generalized Modus Ponens to derive a ground conclusion from a general rule and specific facts.
exercises.prompt: Given the rule $\forall x:\text{Student}(x)\wedge\text{Registered}(x,\text{AI})\Rightarrow\text{MustSubmitHomework}(x)$ and facts $\text{Student}(\text{Priya})$, $\text{Registered}(\text{Priya},\text{AI})$, apply Generalized Modus Ponens to derive a conclusion.
hints: Identify $p_1'=\text{Student}(\text{Priya})$, $p_2'=\text{Registered}(\text{Priya},\text{AI})$ (the known facts) and $p_1=\text{Student}(x)$, $p_2=\text{Registered}(x,\text{AI})$ (the rule's premises).

Find $\theta$ unifying both pairs simultaneously: $\theta=\{x/\text{Priya}\}$ works for both, since $\text{Student}(x)\theta=\text{Student}(\text{Priya})=p_1'$ and $\text{Registered}(x,\text{AI})\theta=\text{Registered}(\text{Priya},\text{AI})=p_2'$.

exercises.objective: Explain the practical tradeoff between forward and backward chaining for FOL.
exercises.prompt: Explain why forward chaining is described as 'data-driven' and backward chaining as 'goal-driven,' and give one situation where each is the more natural choice.
hints: Forward chaining starts from all currently-known facts and fires whatever rules apply, regardless of whether the results are relevant to any particular question, exactly like automatic/unconscious processing (e.g. recognizing an object without deliberately asking 'is this an object?').

Backward chaining starts from a specific query and only explores what's needed to answer *that* query, exactly like deliberate problem-solving (e.g. 'where are my keys?' only pursues leads relevant to finding keys, not everything you could possibly infer from your surroundings).

Forward chaining is natural when you want *all* consequences of new information (e.g. updating a knowledge base after new sensor data); backward chaining is natural when you have one specific question and want to avoid the wasted work of deriving lots of irrelevant facts along the way.
